fixed_statement:
Let \((T_t)\) be a \(\nu\)-symmetric Markov semigroup on \(L^2(\nu)\), and let \(\mathcal E\) be its closed Dirichlet form. Assume that the only zero-energy functions in the domain of \(\mathcal E\) are constants.

Every \(T_t\)-invariant probability measure \(\mu\) with \(\mu\ll\nu\) equals \(\nu\).

For the Gibbs measure
\[
\nu(dv)=Z^{-1}e^{2\Phi(v)}\gamma(dv)
\]
on \(E=C_0([0,1])\), the zero-energy condition holds for the gradient form
\[
\mathcal E(F,G)=\frac12\int_E\langle DF,DG\rangle_H\,d\nu
\]
provided the limiting semigroup is the symmetric semigroup associated with this form.
fixed_proof: For the abstract semigroup, Lemma 9.3 shows that the density \(h=d\mu/d\nu\) equals \(1\), hence \(\mu=\nu\). For the displayed Gibbs gradient form, Lemma 9.4 verifies the zero-energy condition under the stated association of the limiting semigroup with the form.
